ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: To explore the effect of aquaporin NtPIP on crop waterlogging tolerance, a research group measured the root cell respiration rate and oxygen concentration of wild-type (WT) rapeseed and NtPIP gene overexpression lines (OE) under normal oxygen supply (AT) and low oxygen (HT, simulating waterlogging) conditions, and the results are shown in Figure 1. According to Figure 1, under low-oxygen stress, will overexpression of the NtPIP gene enhance or weaken aerobic respiration in root cells?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: To explore the effect of aquaporin NtPIP on crop waterlogging tolerance, a research group measured the root cell respiration rate and oxygen concentration of wild-type (WT) rapeseed and NtPIP gene overexpression lines (OE) under normal oxygen supply (AT) and low oxygen (HT, simulating waterlogging) conditions, and the results are shown in Figure 1. According to Figure 1, under low-oxygen stress, will overexpression of the NtPIP gene enhance or weaken aerobic respiration in root cells?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: Figure 1 contains two bar charts. The vertical axis of the bar chart on the left is root cell respiration rate. Under low-oxygen HT conditions, the WT bar is about 2 μmol O2·min^-1·kg^-1, while the OE bar is about above 7, significantly higher than WT. The vertical axis of the bar chart on the right is oxygen concentration. Under HT conditions, the WT oxygen concentration bar is about 50 μmol·L^-1, and OE is about 140 μmol·L^-1, also significantly higher than WT. Then reason: The question requires comparing the aerobic respiration situation of the NtPIP overexpression line OE and wild-type WT root cells under low-oxygen stress HT. Because under HT conditions the respiration rate of OE is significantly higher than that of WT, and the root oxygen concentration is also higher, this indicates that overexpression of the NtPIP gene improves oxygen supply and increases the aerobic respiration level. Therefore, under low-oxygen stress, overexpression of the NtPIP gene will enhance aerobic respiration in root cells.
